ideas.title: Agent-native interfaces need a formal design science, not just engineering hacks.
ideas.body: The Evolving Agent Interfaces paper shows agents are still constrained by human-oriented UIs — typing cell-by-cell when code would do, paginating through thousands of lines [Evolving Agent Interfaces]. What's missing is a theory of *agent-interface co-design*: how to automatically discover, negotiate, and version machine-readable interfaces between agents and software. This connects to Figma's critique that MCP "is not a perfect protocol" [TechCrunch AI] and Anthropic's decision to replace Git for agent-driven source control [Simon Willison]. The gap: no benchmark or formal framework exists for measuring "interface efficiency" — the ratio of agent capability to interface friction. Signal: Evolving Agent Interfaces, Figma MCP critique, Anthropic source control redesign.

ideas.title: The 4D world-model gap between video generation and explicit simulation is closing — but no one owns the latent bridge.
ideas.body: AEON unifies video and 3D world models [AEON], Latent Bridge maps video latents directly to geometry without RGB decoding [Latent Bridge], and the Video-Point Model forecasts 4D point trajectories across cameras [Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting]. Each solves a piece, but the research gap is a *shared latent representation* that simultaneously supports appearance, geometry, physics, and multi-agent consistency. OverSeer's multi-agent world model [OverSeer] hints at the need. Why now: robotics and embodied agents need world models that are both visually rich and physically actionable, and current approaches force a lossy round-trip. Signal: AEON, Latent Bridge, VPM, OverSeer.

ideas.title: Decision models in LLM systems are systematically unevaluated for context-sensitivity.
ideas.body: DecisionPivot argues that item accuracy alone can't establish whether routing, guardrail, and verification models make correct decisions *across contexts* [DecisionPivot]. This is a direct research gap: current evals treat decision models as classifiers, not as components whose failures cascade. Combine this with the embedded evaluator skepticism from Hugging Face's policy chief [TechCrunch AI] and Microsoft's warning that agents behave like insider threats [TechCrunch AI]. The direction: *contextual decision theory for LLM systems* — how to measure and guarantee decision quality under distribution shift, adversarial prompts, and multi-agent interaction. Signal: DecisionPivot, embedded evaluator critique, Microsoft agent threat warning.

ideas.title: Tactile-visual-language alignment is an under-exploited frontier for physical AI.
ideas.body: Touch-JEPA learns tactile representations from hand-object video with limited supervision [Touch-JEPA], and SenseAlign aligns vision, touch, and language at test time [SenseAlign]. The gap: no foundation model yet unifies these modalities for downstream manipulation tasks, and current approaches treat touch as auxiliary rather than primary. With Eka Robotics demonstrating human-like picking [TechCrunch AI] and "Physical AI in its LEGO era" [TechCrunch AI], there's a clear research opening for *tactile-first world models* that predict contact dynamics from visual and linguistic context. Signal: Touch-JEPA, SenseAlign, Eka Robotics, physical AI commentary.

ideas.title: Flow-based language models are technically promising but lack a killer application.
ideas.body: Large Flow Language Models show parallel generation with control and acceleration tools unavailable to discrete diffusion [Large Flow Language Models], and a hybrid diffusion-autoregressive framework addresses the sequentiality bottleneck [Beyond the Sequentiality Bottleneck]. Yet no paper demonstrates *why* a practitioner should switch from autoregressive decoding for reasoning-heavy workloads. The research gap: flow models for *interactive* generation — where users or agents want to insert, revise, or branch mid-generation, something autoregressive models handle awkwardly. This connects to agent interfaces and the need for non-linear generation. Signal: Large Flow Language Models, hybrid diffusion-autoregressive framework.

ideas.title: Scientific exploration agents need composition benchmarks, not just task benchmarks.
ideas.body: Sage-A1.5 demonstrates "capability composition" for long-horizon scientific work [Sage-A1.5], and GBClaw applies agentic AI to grain boundary discovery [GBClaw]. But the field lacks a rigorous way to measure *when* composing capabilities helps versus hurts — the Capable Teacher, Myopic Scorer paper shows on-policy distillation fails due to compounding errors [Capable Teacher, Myopic Scorer]. The research gap: *compositional generalization in agentic science* — how to predict which sub-capabilities transfer, and how to detect and repair capability interference. Signal: Sage-A1.5, GBClaw, Capable Teacher Myopic Scorer.

ideas.title: Cache engineering for agents is a systems problem hiding in plain sight.
ideas.body: Cache Engineering for Agents notes that as agent trajectories grow, KV cache management becomes the bottleneck [Cache Engineering for Agents], while the Token-Energy Law quantifies joules per token from active bytes [Token-Energy Law]. The gap: no open-source framework treats agent trajectory caching as a first-class optimization target — with semantic compression, hierarchical eviction, and cross-agent cache sharing. This is directly relevant to the million-agent superintelligence question being debated [LessWrong]. Signal: Cache Engineering for Agents, Token-Energy Law, million-agent debate.

ideas.title: Debate-based oversight has a hidden asymmetry: humans improve, AI judges don't.
ideas.body: The paper "Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate, but Weaker AI Models Do Not" [Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate] reveals a critical failure mode for scalable oversight. If weaker models can't be corrected through debate, then debate-based safety protocols that rely on AI judges are fundamentally flawed. The research gap: *asymmetric debate protocols* where the judge's correction mechanism differs from the debaters' — or where debate is used to train judges rather than to evaluate arguments. This connects directly to the AI safety via debate literature and the LessWrong discussion of updatelessness [LessWrong]. Signal: Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate, updatelessness discussion.

ideas.title: Copyright leakage in video generation is measurable but unaddressed as a design constraint.
ideas.body: Copyright Leakage Detection in AI Generated Videos [Copyright Leakage Detection] shows detection is possible, but no work treats leakage prevention as a training objective. With Spotify purging 50 million AI slop tracks [The Verge AI] and Meta pausing Muse sharing after chat leaks [The Verge AI], there's a gap for *provable non-leakage generation* — models that can guarantee no verbatim reproduction of training data in outputs. This is a research problem, not just a policy one. Signal: Copyright Leakage Detection, Spotify slop purge, Muse sharing pause.

ideas.title: An "interface compiler" for agents — automatically generating machine-readable interfaces from human UIs.
ideas.body: The Evolving Agent Interfaces paper demonstrates agents are bottlenecked by human-designed interfaces [Evolving Agent Interfaces]. A product that automatically instruments existing software (spreadsheets, dashboards, CRMs) with agent-native APIs — discovering what operations are possible, generating code-level access patterns, and versioning them — would unlock massive agent productivity gains. Why now: enterprises are deploying agents against legacy software, and the MCP debate [TechCrunch AI] shows protocol standardization is still contested. Who benefits: any company running agents on internal tools; agent platform vendors. Signal: Evolving Agent Interfaces, Figma MCP critique.

ideas.title: A "world-model middleware" for robotics and simulation — one API for video, geometry, and physics.
ideas.body: AEON [AEON], Latent Bridge [Latent Bridge], and VPM [Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting] each solve a piece of the world-model puzzle. A startup that packages these into a unified API — "give me a consistent 4D representation of this scene, with appearance, geometry, and physics" — would serve robotics companies, game studios, and embodied AI labs that don't want to maintain three separate model stacks. Why now: Eka Robotics shows physical AI is commercially viable [TechCrunch AI], and "Physical AI is in its LEGO era" [TechCrunch AI] means the building blocks are ready but not assembled. Signal: AEON, Latent Bridge, VPM, Eka Robotics.

ideas.title: A "tactile data marketplace" for physical AI training.
ideas.body: Touch-JEPA [Touch-JEPA] and SenseAlign [SenseAlign] show tactile learning is data-starved — limited tactile supervision is the bottleneck. A product that collects, cleans, and licenses tactile-visual-language datasets from real robot deployments would be the "Scale AI for touch." Why now: dexterous manipulation is the next frontier [Learning Adaptable Dexterous Skills], and Eka's success shows demand for human-like manipulation [TechCrunch AI]. Who benefits: robotics startups, foundation model labs training physical AI. Signal: Touch-JEPA, SenseAlign, Eka Robotics, dexterous skills paper.

ideas.title: A "decision-model observability" platform for LLM systems.
ideas.body: DecisionPivot shows decision models (routers, guardrails, verifiers) are evaluated on accuracy but not context-sensitivity [DecisionPivot]. A product that continuously monitors decision models in production — detecting when a router starts making different decisions under distribution shift, or when a guardrail's false-negative rate spikes for certain prompt types — would be the Datadog for LLM decision infrastructure. Why now: enterprises are deploying multi-model LLM systems with decision layers, and Microsoft's insider threat warning [TechCrunch AI] shows the risk is real. Signal: DecisionPivot, Microsoft agent threat warning.

ideas.title: A "cache-aware agent runtime" for long-horizon autonomous systems.
ideas.body: Cache Engineering for Agents [Cache Engineering for Agents] and the Token-Energy Law [Token-Energy Law] show that cache management is the hidden cost driver for agents. A runtime that automatically compresses, shares, and evicts KV cache across multi-agent trajectories — with semantic awareness of what's worth keeping — would reduce inference costs by an order of magnitude for long-horizon agents. Why now: the million-agent debate [LessWrong] and Anthropic's $80B loss [Hacker News] make cost efficiency existential. Who benefits: agent platform vendors, enterprises running fleets of agents. Signal: Cache Engineering for Agents, Token-Energy Law, Anthropic loss.

ideas.title: A "debate-as-a-service" oversight tool for high-stakes AI decisions.
ideas.body: The finding that humans improve through debate but weaker AI models don't [Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate] suggests a product: structured debate protocols where humans are the judges, and AI systems are the debaters — for medical, legal, or financial decisions where the cost of error is high but the human judge can be trained through exposure to debates. This inverts the current "AI judge" paradigm. Why now: AI safety via debate is a hot research area [LessWrong], and enterprises need oversight mechanisms that actually work. Signal: Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate, AI safety via debate.

ideas.title: A "generative retrieval" search engine for evolving semantic indexes.
ideas.body: Evolving Semantic Indexes for Generative Retrieval [Evolving Semantic Indexes] shows SID design largely determines generative retrieval quality, but current approaches are static. A product that continuously evolves semantic indexes as user behavior and content change — treating search as a living system rather than a fixed index — would outperform both traditional search and static generative retrieval. Why now: generative retrieval is maturing, and the gap between static and adaptive indexing is widening. Signal: Evolving Semantic Indexes for Generative Retrieval.

ideas.title: A "non-leakage" content generation API for regulated industries.
ideas.body: Copyright Leakage Detection [Copyright Leakage Detection] shows video models can reproduce training data, and Spotify's 50M slop purge [The Verge AI] shows platforms are cracking down. A product that guarantees generated content is provably non-infringing — with leakage detection built into the generation pipeline — would serve media companies, advertising agencies, and game studios that can't risk copyright lawsuits. Why now: copyright enforcement is ramping up, and current generation tools offer no guarantees. Signal: Copyright Leakage Detection, Spotify slop purge.

ideas.title: The "million agents create superintelligence" thesis is wrong — the bottleneck is interface, not agent count.
ideas.body: The debate about whether a million parallel agents can create superintelligence [LessWrong] assumes that scaling agent count is the path. But Evolving Agent Interfaces [Evolving Agent Interfaces] shows agents are bottlenecked by human interfaces, and Cache Engineering for Agents [Cache Engineering for Agents] shows infrastructure costs explode with trajectory length. Prediction: by end of 2027, no system with >10,000 agents will demonstrate superlinear capability gains over a well-engineered 100-agent system. Falsifiable: measure capability per agent as a function of agent count, controlling for interface quality. Signal: million-agent debate, Evolving Agent Interfaces, Cache Engineering.

ideas.title: Open-weights models will not close the gap with frontier models — but they will dominate agentic workloads.
ideas.body: The Interconnects analysis of open models [Interconnects] and the "worse-than-China open weight models" observation [Import AI] suggest open models lag on raw capability. But agentic workloads are bottlenecked by interface and infrastructure, not raw intelligence — and open models allow custom fine-tuning for specific interfaces. Prediction: by mid-2027, open-weights models will power >60% of production agent deployments, even while frontier models win benchmarks. Falsifiable: survey enterprise agent deployments and measure model provenance. Signal: Interconnects open model analysis, Evolving Agent Interfaces, Import AI 476.

ideas.title: Tactile sensing will be more important than vision for the next robotics breakthrough.
ideas.body: The field is obsessed with vision-language models for robotics [UniWALM], but Touch-JEPA [Touch-JEPA] and SenseAlign [SenseAlign] show tactile learning is the under-exploited modality. Eka Robotics' human-like picking [TechCrunch AI] likely relies on force feedback more than vision. Prediction: the next major robotics milestone (e.g., reliable in-hand manipulation of novel objects) will come from a lab that prioritizes tactile data collection over visual data. Falsifiable: track the modality composition of training data for the next breakthrough manipulation system. Signal: Touch-JEPA, SenseAlign, Eka Robotics, dexterous skills paper.

ideas.title: Debate-based AI safety will be abandoned as a primary oversight mechanism within 18 months.
ideas.body: The finding that weaker AI models don't improve through debate [Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate] undermines the core assumption of scalable oversight via debate. Combined with the LessWrong discussion of updatelessness [LessWrong] and the embedded evaluator skepticism [TechCrunch AI], the field is heading toward a crisis in AI-judged oversight. Prediction: by end of 2027, no major AI lab will rely on debate between AI systems as a primary safety mechanism; instead, they'll use human-in-the-loop protocols with AI-assisted evidence gathering. Falsifiable: track safety protocols in frontier lab publications and policy documents. Signal: Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate, embedded evaluator critique, updatelessness discussion.

ideas.title: "Physical AI" will have its ChatGPT moment not from a foundation model, but from a data flywheel.
ideas.body: The "Physical AI is in its LEGO era" framing [TechCrunch AI] assumes a foundation model will unlock robotics. But the bottleneck is data, not architecture — Touch-JEPA's limited supervision problem [Touch-JEPA] and the need for simulation-ready scenes [SceneRig] point to data scarcity. Prediction: the robotics breakthrough will come from a company that builds a self-improving data collection loop (robots collecting their own training data), not from a lab that trains a bigger model. Falsifiable: track whether the next breakthrough system's training data was human-collected or robot-collected. Signal: Physical AI LEGO era, Touch-JEPA, SceneRig, Eka Robotics.

ideas.title: The "agent interface" problem will create a new platform war bigger than the OS wars.
ideas.body: Evolving Agent Interfaces [Evolving Agent Interfaces] shows agents need machine-readable interfaces, and Figma's MCP critique [TechCrunch AI] shows the current protocol is contested. This is analogous to the early days of operating systems — whoever controls the interface standard controls the ecosystem. Prediction: by 2028, there will be 2-3 competing agent-interface standards (like Windows vs. Mac vs. Linux), and the winner will be determined by enterprise adoption, not technical merit. Falsifiable: track the number of production agent deployments on each interface standard. Signal: Evolving Agent Interfaces, Figma MCP critique, Anthropic source control redesign.

ideas.title: Anthropic's compute crisis and the $45B Nscale deal.
ideas.body: Anthropic's $80B net loss [Hacker News], the messy cloud partnerships [TechCrunch AI], and the reported $45B Nscale deal [TechCrunch AI] suggest a compute crunch that could reshape the AI landscape. Watch whether Anthropic's IPO [Simon Willison] changes its compute strategy, and whether the CoreWeave debt distress [The Verge AI] spreads to other AI infrastructure providers.

ideas.title: The "Evolving Agent Interfaces" paper's downstream impact.
ideas.body: This paper [Evolving Agent Interfaces] could be the "Attention Is All You Need" of agent-interface research. Watch for follow-up work on interface discovery, interface versioning, and whether frontier labs start publishing their internal interface specifications.

ideas.title: The debate oversight crisis.
ideas.body: The finding that weaker AI models don't improve through debate [Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate] could trigger a rethink of AI safety protocols. Watch for responses from OpenAI, Anthropic, and DeepMind on whether they're revising their debate-based oversight approaches.

ideas.title: The US-China model cold war.
ideas.body: The US order to remove DeepSeek from federal systems [TechCrunch AI] and the "American-made models" push [Interconnects] suggest a bifurcating AI ecosystem. Watch whether this accelerates open-weights development outside the US, and whether Chinese labs respond with their own restrictions.

ideas.title: The "Physical AI" funding wave.
ideas.body: Eka Robotics' $1.45B valuation [TechCrunch AI], the "LEGO era" framing [TechCrunch AI], and the dexterous skills research [Learning Adaptable Dexterous Skills] suggest a robotics investment wave is building. Watch for a major acquisition or IPO in the physical AI space that validates the thesis.

ideas.title: The "cache engineering" research agenda.
ideas.body: Cache Engineering for Agents [Cache Engineering for Agents] and the Token-Energy Law [Token-Energy Law] open a new systems research direction. Watch for whether this becomes a standard topic at systems conferences (OSDI, SOSP, MLSys) and whether frontier labs publish their internal cache management techniques.

ideas.title: The "generative retrieval" commercialization.
ideas.body: Evolving Semantic Indexes [Evolving Semantic Indexes] suggests generative retrieval is maturing. Watch for a startup or major lab productizing generative retrieval for search or recommendation, and whether it displaces traditional embedding-based retrieval.

ideas.title: The "tactile data" gold rush.
ideas.body: Touch-JEPA [Touch-JEPA] and SenseAlign [SenseAlign] show tactile learning is data-starved. Watch for a company or lab that starts collecting tactile data at scale — this would be the "ImageNet moment" for touch.
